crm_labels.max_extend_days: Can be postponed by at most (days)

session_init.note: Called once at the start of the call - the response is the context directly

args.reason: The system did not answer; a member of staff will follow up

confirms_pay.desc: The customer confirms they will pay on the original date, with no conditions

reschedule_request.desc: Still intends to pay, but asks to move the date (not a refusal of the debt)
cues: I won't have it by tomorrow, could we make it Friday?
My customer is paying me soon, could I have a little longer?

gives_date.desc: The customer names the date they will pay
cues: Could I make it next month?

confirms_new_date.desc: Confirms the new date that was offered

already_paid.desc: Claims to have paid already - a dispute about status, not a refusal
cues: Check again, I made the transfer

asks_human.desc: Asks for a real person, or asks something outside the payment flow
cues: Could I speak to a person?
Could I change to another model?

no_input.desc: Silence, or an answer that is not interpretable speech

declarations.name: check_new_date
declarations.desc: Check whether the date the customer asked to move to is within the shop's limit (no more than max_extend_days from due_date) - returns {in_range: bool, valid_dates: [...], max_extend_days: n}, where valid_dates are the acceptable dates (including the one the customer asked for, if in_range=true). Call it every time the customer names a date; never decide this yourself

date.desc: The date the customer named, converted to canonical form before sending

gating.note: Call it only once the customer has named a date - if there is no date yet, ask with ask_new_date first and never call it with an empty date. Counting days is the system's job, not the agent's

in_range.desc: Is the requested date within the limit?

max_extend_days.desc: The maximum number of days it can be moved by

new_date.desc: The date once checked - the same name as the slot in the line

declarations.name: record_call_result
declarations.desc: Record the call outcome - always called before the closing reply

new_date.desc: The new payment date the customer confirmed - required when result=rescheduled; use the value check_new_date returned

reason.desc: The reason for this call's outcome (filled in by the system when session_init does not answer)

states.note: Remind them one day ahead, then wait for the answer - never call record_call_result on the first turn

on.note: The customer asks to postpone and names the date in the same sentence - skip asking for the date
Silent from the start = could not be reached; a member of staff will follow up

states.note: Once the customer names a date, call check_new_date before answering, then pick the line from the result: in_range=true -> confirm_new_date (9004); in_range=false -> date_too_far (9005), then wait for a new date

on.note: The customer offers another date - check it again

outcome.desc: Confirms they will pay on the original date
The payment date was moved and the new date confirmed
The customer claims to have paid - waiting for the backend to check
Passed to a member of staff (asked for a person / out of scope / could not be reached)

constraints.desc: **Never decide for yourself whether the date the customer asked for is within the limit** - call `check_new_date(date)` every time the customer names a date, then read `in_range` and `valid_dates` from the result. `in_range=true` -> say `confirm_new_date` (9004); `in_range=false` -> say `date_too_far` (9005). Counting days is the system's job

**Always confirm the new date before recording it** - after `confirm_new_date` (9004), wait for the customer to accept before calling `record_call_result(result="rescheduled", new_date=…)`. **Never record the moment the customer mentions a date**, because that date has not been confirmed yet
**`new_date` must be the value `check_new_date` returned** - never type what the customer said verbatim, and never leave it empty when result=rescheduled

**The customer claims to have paid** -> say `close_paid_claim` (9007), record result=paid_claimed and end the call. **Never argue, never ask for proof, never keep chasing** - checking is the backend's job

**The customer asks for a person, or asks about something outside the payment flow** (changing model, promotions, and so on) -> say `close_handoff` (9008), record result=handoff and end the call. **Never try to answer it yourself**
**Silence is not consent** - a customer who answers '...' or '(silence)' is the `no_input` event and nothing else; never treat it as confirms_pay and never record result=confirmed
**One sentence at a time**, chosen from the catalog only. Never write your own text, and never repeat the amount or the due date after the opening line has given them
Say how many days it can be moved by at most twice per call - once that is used and the customer still offers a date beyond the limit, close with close_handoff (9008) and pass it to a member of staff

Never call record_call_result before the customer has said they confirm, want to postpone, or have already paid - a greeting on picking up (hello / hi / yes?) and silence at the start of the call do not count as an answer; greet and give the due date first

catalog.template: Hello [customer_name], [shop_name] is calling with a reminder. Tomorrow, [due_date], an instalment of [amount] baht falls due. Can we look out for your transfer tomorrow?
Thank you [customer_name]. We have noted that [amount] baht will arrive tomorrow. If anything changes, just give us a call. Goodbye.
Of course. Which day would suit you for the payment?
Noted. We will move the due date to [new_date]. Shall I confirm that?
I'm sorry, we can only move the date by up to [max_extend_days] days. Would another date within that work?
Thank you. The new payment date is recorded as [new_date]. Goodbye.
Noted. Let us check the amount in our system first. If we do not find it, we will call you back. Thank you.
I will have a member of staff contact you. Thank you.
I'm sorry, could you say that again?
catalog.hint: Used when the customer was not heard or understood - the fallback line for any point in the call

auxiliary_templates.note: A template not tied to a state - it can be said at any point in the call
